title: Combine factors of production

blocks.heading: Combine factors of production
blocks.text: Land, labour and capital provide natural resources, human effort and productive resources used to create goods and services. A missing necessary input can prevent other available inputs being used; enterprise organises the combination. An invented bakery needs a site and water, people with time and skills, and produced equipment such as an oven. Having an oven is insufficient if there is no water or no one able to operate it. Identify what a case actually lacks rather than recommending more of a resource already available.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Land as a factor
blocks.text: Land means natural resources used in production, including physical space, water, minerals and soil. The productive role of land depends on the quality, location and accessibility of the relevant resource. In economic language, land is wider than a plot on a map. Fish stocks and mineral deposits are natural resources even though they are not cultivated fields. A building on a site is a produced asset; the physical site is the natural-resource input. Keep the distinction tied to how the resource arose.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Labour
blocks.text: Labour is human physical and mental effort used in production. Skills, health, available time and organisation influence how labour contributes to output. A worker measuring timber uses mental effort as well as physical movement. A teacher provides a service through knowledge, preparation and communication. The number of workers alone does not show their productive capacity: training, equipment and other necessary inputs matter.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Capital: finance and produced assets
blocks.text: Capital in production must distinguish money capital, the finance available for acquiring resources, from capital goods, the produced assets used to make goods or services. Finance can acquire productive equipment and other inputs, but the finance and the equipment perform different roles. A sewing group may have money but lack a machine, or possess a machine but lack money for cloth. Identify which role the question concerns before explaining how capital helps production. Here, capital does not mean a country’s main city.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Remove a missing input
blocks.text: A fictional bakery has trained workers, a working oven, flour and orders. Its water connection fails. Restoring safe water is the immediate productive priority: the available labour and equipment cannot make the required dough without it. Another oven would leave the missing water input unresolved. This case combines the factors rather than asking for another list. If the oven instead failed while water remained available, the recommended action would change.
